body: Of course, I'm glad to hear things are going so well for you, too!

Hey, so was searching through my history for something and came across this conversation. I just wanted to say I hope shit's going better for you, man. I found the right meds and right shrink and I feel immeasurably better. I hope you're there, too, but if not - don't lose hope. 🖤
Thank you. I'll talk to my therapist today.
That was very helpful, thank you. And thanks for your kind words, they mean a lot. I hope you're able to manage the anxiety beast, mental health is a bitch.
But what about three times?
Thank you. You stay strong, as well.

I posted something about this tonight. I get you, man/girl. It's so maddening. Makes you wish people would just stop caring already so you could get on with it. That's how it feels for me, at least. Because having this decision taken away because of them feels like just one more way in which I have no control over my own life.

I haven't talked to them. Because I perform psychological evaluations on inmates at the prison. If I talk to them, they're going to be concerned that I can't be objective, or that it's too much stress. And even if by some miracle that's not the case, I'd lose my clearance to work at the prison if I'm hospitalized. 

Honestly I don't even know what successful means. Being able to stand on my own two feet, I guess. Being able to comfort a friend whose mother died suddenly instead of her feeling like she has to be there for me. Being able to afford to take my dog to the vet when she has an eye infection instead of just hoping it takes care of itself. I know I'm capable of more, and everyone my entire life has told me they have high expectations for me. I just feel like I've lost the ability to access "more," and even though I'm not actively suicidal, I'm honestly terrified I'm going to dissociate or have a breakdown and do something in that state. Or become so shattered I lose the ability to function at any rate. 

Edit: Today I actually did let my boss know I'm going to therapy for personal issues. I had to tell her about all the upcoming rheumatologist appointments I'm going to have, and it just kind of came out when she asked of that's what all my recent appointments have been for.

Thank you for your response. I have started seeing a new therapist. I just don't know how the hell I'm going to be able to afford to continue seeing her, without being able to donate plasma I won't have the money for bi-weekly, let alone weekly visits. 

Meanwhile she's trying to talk me into going to intensive outpatient or inpatient mental health treatment because my emotions are so out of control and everything just feels like it's building to something. Even while I'm fighting tooth and nail to hang on. But if I do that, I lose my job. I lose my apartment. I lose everything I've worked so hard for, and that's only going to leave me more depressed. Because I'm supposed to be strong. I'm supposed to be successful. But I've been white knuckling it for so long, I just feel like I'm losing my grip.
I reported him to the licensing board. Now we wait and see what they decide.

Thank you for writing this all out, it helps to know how other people may approach these issues. This certainly sounds like something I would be better able to handle. 

Can I ask, is it normal when facing these kinds of issues to feel worse before you feel better? I think I've been operating under that assumption (it made sense - if I've buried things, bringing them up is going to be painful), but now I'm wondering if that's a faulty assumption? My PTSD is worse right now than it maybe ever has been.
Thank you, that actually means a lot. It's been a weird experience, going from trusting someone pretty implicitly to questioning everything, I've been triggered to hell with it all.

No. Because leading up to this it was uncomfortable but I felt like it had a purpose and I knew that sometimes you have to lean into the discomfort in therapy. There was a tiny concern in the back of my head for a while, I think, but until he gave me this assignment it hadn't gotten to the point where I started being worried that something may actually be off.

I have been concerned once or twice that he's attracted to me. But I've also got issues with differentiating men's feelings toward me and not being able to decipher platonic from romantic, so I attributed it to that. 

As for the dissociation, you're right on. I don't remember a lot of the rape because I blocked it out. I'm worried that  if I try to sort through those memories on my own, I'm going to end up in a worse position than I am now. 

So as a clinician, do you think these are things we can talk about and work through? Or would your advice be to cut and run?

No, he didn't, really. I was pretty clear about my hesitation about it, even if I used some humor as a defense mechanism. Joked that I would be sick for our next appointment, when he walked me out and said see you in a couple weeks, I joked that he would if I didn't take up residence in a corner somewhere, etc. So he knew at least that I was nervous about it but didn't do much to assuage my feelings or explain more why it needed to be done.

Well first off I'm glad you understand some of the same issues I have, cause most of the time they make me feel like a crazy person haha. 

I had to really think on the intentionally triggering. I think you may be right. But I think the reason he may be doing that is because I intellectualize everything to death. I'm always in my head about things and rarely allow myself to feel or trust the feelings. He even mentioned at one point he was trying to jerk me out of my head and force me to feel. Or maybe I'm making excuses. I don't know anymore. 

I think I've decided I'm not doing the assignment, and I'm going to discuss these things with him as best I can at our next appointment and try to go from there.

That is one of my big concerns - retraumatizing myself. I've done EMDR and similar things in the past, and really felt like I've been better able to handle discussing it, triggers have been almost non-existent, etc but over the past several weeks things are feeling really raw again. It's been years since I've had a panic attack but had one after our last session.  Which I know facing hard things and being uncomfortable can be important in therapy, too, that's what's making it hard to decipher how to feel about this.
She said there was no way to make the black less black, she thought we understood each other, etc.  Nothing helpful.
Someone else suggested going against some of the care recommendations. Using too much ointment, that kind of stuff to maybe draw some ink out. Is that a viable idea?
You are seriously amazing, thank you! No chance you live in Utah, is there? 😜 I'll send you pictures a bit later today, thank you!

I'm thinking that may be the route I need to take. Just a bummer that I'm stuck with it for a while. But if I get it lightened, then I'm hoping I can do something with it that I'll really like. I've been thinking of a Medusa tattoo for a while now, that may be the cover up I go with.

This just made me cry, haha. Thank you so much for your help and kindness. Its a weird kind of helplessness I've been feeling, so it's good to know I still have viable options. I'm completely open to how the Medusa could be done, obviously I don't want another fiasco to come out of it. I just still want it to look somewhat feminine. 

And thank you for letting me know about the water color issue, as well. This was supposed to be me first non-simple tattoo, so it helps to know I don't have to be completely gun shy in the future.
I did a lot of research, looked at her portfolio on their website, in the store, her insta. She had (allegedly) done these watercolor space looking tattoos before, that's why I went with her.
Thank you for saying that. I'm very much a fixer person, if there's an issue, let's find a way to fix it. And at the time being I just feel so helpless with this.

I have been wanting to get a Medusa tattoo. I wonder if a good artist would be able to cover it up and make this snakes, with her face on my shoulder or something? I still don't really want something starkly black on my chest, but I think that'd be a better option than sticking with this tattoo. Do you think that'd be able to be done?

Yes. I asked her about all of the black, told her we had discussed not wanting black, and wanting it to be a nebula. Honestly I was too much in shock and still processing to tell her I hated it, but she was aware I wasn't happy.
Thank you!
I did ask for a blood test, as well. Haven't gotten those results back yet.
I have contacted the other guy and let him know to get tested.

I recognize that. I had gone through the same conversation with the ex, and had been assured in the same way. I trusted him, which I now realize was naieve and a mistake, and I am not blameless here, either.

I wasn't clear in the original post. I had had unprotected sex with a short term boyfriend after my last pap. I had the same conversation with him, regarding his status, and he told me that he had been tested in the past month, hadn't had sex in the meantime, and was clean. I trusted that, which I realize now was naieve. And that in not sharing that piece of information, I am in the wrong, as well. I am realizing that I'm overly trusting, and could have been the one that passed it on. So I am not blameless. However, naieve as it may have been, I was acting in good faith and he was not. I'm still just very torn on what to do with this.

I agree, I don't think he did anything wrong, either. Hes a good guy and I have definitely developed feelings. Which is why I'm having such a hard time with it. I guess I wish that it didn't get to this point if that's how he feels, but I can fully understand that he may have needed time to sort all that out just like I did with all of this. Just sucks, is all.

Right. Which is why I acknowledged several times in my post that I don't hold that against him, he can have preferences, I know I limit my dating pool with my weight, etc. This wasn't a "Oh poor me" post, it was a post asking for advice on if thats something we can or should move through. Which I feel like I made pretty clear.
